dominant_breach: private contract architecture can individualize small, repeated, or workplace claims so thoroughly that legal rights survive on paper while the economically viable remedy disappears
fastest_washout: class/collective waiver, confidential forum, high proof burden, no public precedent, retaliation fear, and low individual claim value wash out enforcement before liability is reached

remedy_operability_gate.note: A right that cannot be economically enforced by ordinary claimants cannot certify as an effective wealth-protection rule.

arbitration_class_waiver_remedy_suppress.note: Official CFPB, GAO, and controlling legal sources support an active finding that class/collective waiver design can make small recurring harms economically unenforceable.

collective_redress_availability.note: A formal individual forum is not equivalent to collective, representative, or public enforcement when claim value is low, proof is expensive, and repeat harms are dispersed.

private_enforcement_availability.note: Where private enforcement is suppressed, public enforcement must be demonstrably scaled to substitute for lost deterrence and claimant restoration.

public_private_enforcement_mix.note: GAO notes agency paths may remain available in some settings, but missing data and private-right suppression keep the mix uncertified.

claimant_standing_access.note: Standing on paper is weaker than usable forum access, discovery, fee shifting, anti-retaliation, and group claim capacity. Rev0344 unused-source burn-down: OECD access-to-justice evidence is now bound to remedy operability and claimant standing.

remedial_data_logging_and_auditability.note: Confidential or fragmented proceedings make systemic harm hard to see; the cube should score missing arbitration/preclusion data as proof debt.

proof_debt: prevalence of arbitration/class waivers by sector, income, race, job type, and product market

remedy_operability_register.harm_or_claim: Low-value repeated consumer or worker harm made non-viable by arbitration/class waiver design
remedy_operability_register.claimant_perimeter: Workers, consumers, servicemembers, tenants, borrowers, platform users, and others subject to take-it-or-leave-it contract procedure
remedy_operability_register.standing_path: Individual arbitration, agency complaint, limited court routes, or statutory carveout where available
remedy_operability_register.notice_explanation: Contract terms must be visible enough to know forum, waiver, fees, opt-out, and public-enforcement alternatives
remedy_operability_register.interim_protection: Generally weak; the case needs anti-retaliation, fee-shifting, emergency injunctive routes, and preservation of collective claims
remedy_operability_register.time_to_relief: Uncertified because individual claim economics and confidential processes hide abandonment and delay
remedy_operability_register.review_body: Arbitrator, court on threshold enforceability, agency enforcement body, or legislative/regulatory carveout
remedy_operability_register.collective_or_representative_action: Core blocked surface; class, collective, representative, and pattern enforcement must be preserved or substituted
remedy_operability_register.restoration_remedy: Individual damages are insufficient when claim value is low and harm is repeatable; disgorgement, public penalties, injunctive relief, and class/representative repair are needed
remedy_operability_register.enforcement_actor: Courts, arbitrators, CFPB, DOJ, DOL, state AGs, labor agencies, private counsel, and representative organizations

case_notes: rev0332 active finding: forced arbitration is scored as remedy suppression when class/collective waiver design converts legally valid claims into economically irrational individual proceedings.
